title: What is Python & Running Your First Script
learningObjectives: Know where Python is used in the real world.
Differentiate between comments and executable code.
Run a simple Python script successfully.
introduction:
Welcome to your Python journey! 🎉

Every website, mobile app, game, banking system, artificial intelligence model and automation tool is built using programming languages. Python is one of the most popular programming languages in the world because it is easy to learn, powerful and incredibly versatile.

In this lesson, you will write your very first Python program. Don't worry if you've never programmed before. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how Python executes instructions and you'll be able to display messages on the screen using the print() function.

whyLearn.title: Why Learn Python?
content: Python has a simple and readable syntax, making it beginner-friendly.
It is used in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning.
Python powers websites and APIs using frameworks like Django and FastAPI.
It is widely used for cybersecurity and ethical hacking.
Scientists use Python for research and data analysis.
Game developers use Python to build games and prototypes.
Many of the world's biggest companies rely on Python.

didYouKnow.title: Did You Know?
facts: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
Python is named after the comedy group 'Monty Python', not the snake.
Python consistently ranks among the world's most popular programming languages.
Companies like Google, Netflix, Instagram, Spotify and NASA use Python.

sections.heading: What is a Programming Language?
sections.content:
A programming language is a way humans communicate instructions to computers. Just like people use English or Swahili to communicate with each other, programmers use languages like Python to communicate with computers.

Computers cannot understand normal human language directly. Instead, they understand instructions written using programming languages.

sections.heading: What is Python?
sections.content:
Python is a high-level programming language designed to be simple and easy to read. Instead of using complicated symbols everywhere, Python looks almost like plain English.

One reason Python is loved by beginners is because you can focus on solving problems rather than worrying about difficult syntax.

sections.heading: How Python Executes Code
sections.content:
Python executes your program from the first line to the last line.

It reads one instruction, performs it, then moves to the next instruction.

Think of Python as someone carefully following a recipe. It never skips steps unless you tell it to.

sections.heading: The print() Function
sections.content:
The print() function displays information on the screen.

Anything inside the parentheses will appear in the output.

This is the most commonly used function when learning Python because it helps you see what your program is doing.

sections.heading: Strings
sections.content:
A string is simply text.

Strings must always be surrounded by quotation marks.

Python accepts either double quotes or single quotes.

sections.heading: Comments
sections.content:
Comments begin with the # symbol.

Python ignores comments completely.

Comments are used to explain code for humans reading it later.

examples.title: Printing Text
examples.explanation: Python displays exactly what is inside the quotation marks.

examples.title: Multiple print() Statements
examples.explanation: Each print() statement displays its own line.

examples.title: Using Comments
examples.code:
# This is a comment
print("Learning Python")
examples.explanation: Python ignores the comment and only executes the print() statement.

commonMistakes.why: Hello is not inside quotation marks.
Python is case-sensitive. 'Print' is different from 'print'.
Opening and closing quotation marks must match.

debuggingChallenge.question: Why doesn't this program work?
debuggingChallenge.solution: Replace Print with print because Python is case-sensitive.

miniChallenge.title: Your First Program
miniChallenge.description: Create a short program that prints your name, your country and a motivational quote using three separate print() statements.

hints: Remember to put text inside quotation marks.
Use one print() statement for each line.
Python reads your program from top to bottom.

quiz.explanation: Python executes code sequentially from the first line to the last.

summary:
Excellent work! 🎉 You have completed your very first Python lesson.

You learned what Python is, why it is popular, where it is used, how Python executes code, how to use the print() function, how strings work and how comments help explain code.

Most importantly, you've written your first Python program. Every experienced Python developer started with a simple print() statement just like you.
keyTakeaways: Python executes code from top to bottom.
Strings must be enclosed in quotation marks.
Comments begin with # and are ignored by Python.
